about: English meaning written for this library (en-scriptures) from the Sanskrit (tools/meanings/style.md), line by line, in the Advaita tradition of Śaṅkara.

sh1: When the appointed time has come and stands near,
the grammar's “ḍukṛñ karaṇe” will never save you.
sh2: O fool, give up the thirst for gaining wealth;
awaken in your mind a good understanding, free from craving.
Whatever wealth you gain by your own work,
with that keep your mind content.
sh3: Seeing a woman's breasts and navel,
do not fall into the grip of infatuation.
This is only a change of flesh, fat and the like:
reflect on this in your mind again and again.
sh4: Water on a lotus leaf is very unsteady;
Know that the whole world is seized by disease and conceit
sh5: As long as a man is able to earn wealth, so long his own family is fond of him.
Later, when he lives on in a worn-out body,
no one at home asks him even a word.
sh6: As long as the breath dwells in the body,
so long they ask at home after his welfare.
When the breath has gone and the body perishes,
even his wife fears that body.
sh7: The child, so long, is absorbed in play;
the young man, so long, is absorbed in young women;
the old man, so long, is absorbed in worry;
no one at all is absorbed in the supreme Brahman.
sh8: Who is your wife? Who is your son?
Whose are you? Who are you? Where have you come from? Reflect on that truth here, brother.
sh9: From the company of the good comes non-attachment;
from freedom from delusion, steadiness in the unmoving Truth;
from steadiness in the Truth, liberation while living.
sh10: When youth has gone, where is the stir of desire?
When the water has dried, where is the lake?
When wealth is spent, where is the family?
When the Truth is known, where is worldly existence?
sh11: Do not be proud of wealth, people or youth;
time takes away everything in the twinkling of an eye.
Leaving all this, which is made of māyā,
and knowing Brahman, enter the state of Brahman.
sh12: Day and night, evening and morning,
winter and spring come again and again.
Time plays, life goes by; even so, the wind of hope does not let go.
sh13: Why this worry over wife and wealth?
O madman, have you no one to restrain you?
In the three worlds the company of the good alone
becomes the boat for crossing the ocean of worldly existence.
sh13a: In full, through these twelve verses like clusters of flowers,
this teaching was given to the grammarian;
it was given by the one skilled in learning,
sh14: One wears matted locks, one a shaven head, one has his hair plucked out,
one puts on ochre robes and many other garbs:
the fool sees, and yet does not see;
these many garbs are only for the sake of the belly.
sh15: The limbs have grown feeble, the head has turned grey,
the old man walks, holding a staff;
even then he does not let go the lump of his hopes.
sh16: Fire in front, the sun behind;
at night he sits with knees drawn up to the chin;
he begs into his palm and lives under a tree; even then the noose of hope does not let him go.
sh17: One goes on pilgrimage to Gaṅgāsāgara,
keeps vows or gives in charity;
yet, without knowledge, by every view,
he does not gain liberation even in a hundred births.
sh18: Living in a temple or at the foot of a tree,
the bare earth for a bed, a deerskin for a garment,
giving up all possessions and pleasures:
whom does such dispassion not make happy?
sh19: Whether one delights in yoga or in pleasure,
whether one delights in company or is without company,
the one whose mind delights in Brahman
sh20: One who has studied even a little of the Bhagavad Gītā,
drunk even a tiny drop of Gaṅgā water,
with him Yama has no dispute.
sh21: lying again in a mother's womb:
in this worldly existence, so hard to cross and without a shore,
O Murāri, save me by your grace.
sh22: His patched cloak made of rags from the street,
his path beyond merit and sin,
his mind fixed in yoga, the yogī
delights, just like a child or one intoxicated.
sh23: Who are you? Who am I? Where have I come from?
Who is my mother? Who is my father?
Consider thus: all this is without substance;
leave this world aside as the fancy of a dream.
sh24: In you, in me and everywhere else there is one Viṣṇu; unable to bear me, you are angry with me in vain.
if you wish soon to reach the state of Viṣṇu.
sh25: Towards foe or friend, son or kinsman,
make no effort to quarrel or to ally.
and everywhere give up the ignorance that sees difference.
sh26: Giving up desire, anger, greed and delusion,
reflect within yourself: who am I?
Fools without knowledge of the Self are cast down into hell and tormented there.
sh27: The Gītā and the thousand names (of Viṣṇu) should be sung;
the form of the Lord of Śrī should be meditated on without pause;
the mind should be led into the company of the good;
and wealth should be given to the needy.
sh28: For pleasure a man indulges with women;
afterwards, alas, disease comes to the body.
Although in this world death is the final refuge,
even so he does not give up sinful conduct.
sh29: truly, there is not a trace of happiness in it.
The wealthy fear even their own son;
this is the way set everywhere.
sh30: Breath control, withdrawal of the senses,
discerning enquiry into the eternal and the passing,
the practice of samādhi with japa:
do these with care, with great care.
sh31: Wholly devoted to the lotus feet of the Guru,
be free from worldly existence soon.
Thus, by restraint of the senses and the mind,
you will see the Lord who dwells in your own heart.

sh1: “Ḍukṛñ karaṇe” is the entry for the root kr̥, “to do”, in Pāṇini's list of roots. Tradition says Śaṅkara spoke this hymn on seeing an old man in Kāśī learning grammar rules by rote. This verse is the refrain; singers repeat it after every verse.
sh13a: Verses 2–13 are called the Dvādaśa-mañjarikā, “the twelve flower-clusters”; this verse closes them.
sh14: Tradition holds that verses 14–27, the Caturdaśa-mañjarikā, were spoken one each by fourteen disciples of Śaṅkara; this one is ascribed to Padmapāda.
sh17: Gaṅgāsāgara is the place of pilgrimage where the Gaṅgā meets the sea.
sh20: Murāri, “the foe of the demon Mura”, is Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
sh27: Gītā-nāma-sahasram is read as the Bhagavad Gītā and the Viṣṇu Sahasranāma.
